title: Count real tokens in every mini-batch
description: A quick reference for the causal-window, batching, and token-weighted averaging terms used here.

terms.definition: A fixed-length input and shifted-target record that never crosses a document boundary.
A group of training windows whose contributions share one parameter update.
The maximum number of complete windows requested for one batch chunk.
The last batch retained with fewer examples when the epoch remainder is incomplete.
One training-example appearance of a target token, counted separately from matching IDs.
The number of real target occurrences used to average batch loss and gradients.
A parameter-gradient sum divided by the number of actual target-token contributions.
An unnormalized sum retained with its contribution count before final averaging.
A combined mean that weights each accumulated piece by its token count.
A batch containing only real windows, with no synthetic rows or tokens.
